title: Rationalize batch-windowing and provide incremental KV cache migration path
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batch windowing and the KV cache evolution have diverged. The current batch window controller uses multiple heuristics (timer-driven windows, request-count windows, and per-shard backpressure) which interact poorly with the newer epoch-based KV cache index. This produces sporadic latency spikes, KV contention, and complex migration steps when we roll a new on-disk shard layout.

Goal: Consolidate batch-window semantics into a single, deterministic controller and implement an incremental, backwards-compatible migration path for KV cache shards. The work should reduce tail latency, simplify scheduler logic, and enable rolling upgrades without full service disruption.

Scope:
- Replace current heuristic stack with a single epoch-based batch-window controller that exposes a small set of knobs (max_window_ms, max_tokens, latency_slo_ms).
- Implement epoch-aware lease semantics for slots so KV cache reads/writes are coordinated with batch boundaries.
- Add a migration tool and on-the-fly compatibility layer that allows old shard format to be read while writes are upgraded to the new format over time.
- Clean scheduler integration points: remove legacy fast-path branches, centralize slot allocation metrics, and add backpressure signals consumed by the controller.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of the serving runtime or changing model execution kernels. This ticket focuses on orchestration, cache schema migration, and scheduler cleanup only.
acceptance_criteria: New batch-window controller replaces existing heuristics and has >= 95% unit test coverage for window boundary cases
End-to-end load test shows 20% reduction in 99th percentile latency for 4k sequence workloads under mixed bursty traffic
KV cache migration tool can convert a shard online with < 2% additional request latency in canary cluster
Feature flag exists to toggle epoch-based behavior and can be rolled back without cache corruption
No loss of requests during a staged rollout (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitoring dashboards show stable error rates
migration_plan: Phase 1: Merge compatibility layer in runtime that can read both formats and write in legacy mode by default. Phase 2: Deploy to canary (10% traffic) and run conversion tool on a single shard. Phase 3: Enable write-upgrade flag for canary; continue conversion. Phase 4: Expand to 50% then 100% while monitoring metrics and aborting on SLO regressions. Phase 5: Remove legacy read-path after all shards converted and stable for 2 weeks.
deploy_plan: Canary rollout via runtime-1.22: stage canary nodes in us-west, enable feature flag for 10% traffic, run conversion on low-traffic shards overnight, promote to 50% with expanded autoscaling, finally complete full rollout after 72h of no regressions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch boundaries and lease expiry; integration tests with simulated burst loads; chaos test for node restart during migration; nightly load test harness on staging to validate 99th percentile latency and throughput. Create a test suite that replays production traces from the last 30 days to simulate realistic traffic shapes.
observability_changes: Add metrics: batch_window_duration_ms, batch_window_size_tokens, epoch_lease_acquires, kvcache_migration_progress_percent. Add dashboard panels: batch-window heatmap (per-shard), migration progress, slot allocation latency distribution. Emit structured logs for migration steps and lease rejections.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Migration causes unexpected read errors. Mitigation: compatibility layer + schema validation + automated rollback path
Risk: Single new controller introduces regression in rare traffic patterns. Mitigation: feature flag + targeted canary + replayed traces in staging
Risk: Increased CPU from migration conversion. Mitigation: run conversions during off-peak and rate-limit conversion threads
notes:
We evaluated two approaches: (A) immediate in-place upgrade with full downtime window, (B) incremental compatibility-first migration. Chosen approach is B to preserve customer SLAs. The epoch-model gives clearer semantics for coordinating KV cache operations with batching and allowed easier reasoning about backpressure.

Benchmark notes: baseline 99p latency for target workload was 420ms; early prototype cut it to ~320ms under synthetic load with warm cache. More realistic trace replay results pending.
